IN THE CASE OF BOTH AIRCRAFT, NEITHER THE ENGINES NOR THE YOKES HAVE BEEN REMOVED. THIS LED US TO BELIEVE THE BOLTS WERE NOT TORQUED PROPERLY DURING THE PRODUCTION OF THE AIRCRAFT.  WE HAVE WORKED CLOSELY WITH DASSAULT STRUCTURES AND ENGINEERING TO RESOLVE THE ISSUE WITH BOTH AIRCRAFT. DASSAULT RECOMMENDED VISUALLY INSPECTING BORES AND BOLTS, AND IF AVAILABLE, REPLACING THE BOLTS. NORDAM (WHO MANUFACTURES THE YOKES) RECOMMENDED RETORQUING THE BOLT BY FOLLOWING THE INSTALLATION GUIDELINES AND MONITORING THE HARDWARE FOR LOOSENESS.  ALL FOUR BOLTS WERE REMOVED AND REPLACED WITH NEW ONES FOLLOWING THE RECOMMENDED INSPECTIONS. WE WILL CONTINUE TO MONITOR THESE BOLTS FOR TIGHTNESS OVER THE COMING MONTHS.

THE AIRCRAFT LANDED ON RUNWAY 20R AT KSNA UNDER VISUAL METEOROLOGICAL CONDITIONS. NORMAL BRAKING WAS AVAILABLE DURING THE LANDING ROLL USING THE PRIMARY HYDRAULIC BRAKING SYSTEM.

THE AIRCRAFT EXITED THE RUNWAY AT TAXIWAY ECHO AND TURNED LEFT ONTO TAXIWAY ALPHA. IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE TURN ONTO TAXIWAY ALPHA, THE “PWR BRK LOW PRESS” ANNUNCIATOR ILLUMINATED, AND A COMPLETE LOSS OF PRIMARY HYDRAULIC BRAKING WAS OBSERVED.

THE BACKUP BRAKING SYSTEM (PNEUMATIC NITROGEN) WAS IMMEDIATELY SELECTED AND USED TO ARREST FORWARD MOTION. TO ENSURE THE AIRCRAFT CAME TO A COMPLETE STOP AND TO PREVENT FURTHER MOVEMENT, BOTH ENGINES WERE SUBSEQUENTLY SHUT DOWN. ALL EXTERIOR LIGHTS WERE LEFT ON.

KSNA GROUND CONTROL WAS ADVISED THAT THE AIRCRAFT HAD LOST PRIMARY BRAKING, WAS OPERATING ON THE BACKUP BRAKING SYSTEM ONLY, AND WOULD REQUIRE TOWING ASSISTANCE TO THE RAMP.

APPROXIMATELY 10 MINUTES LATER, ACI NORTH ARRIVED, AND THE AIRCRAFT WAS SECURELY ATTACHED TO THE TUG. AFTER THE AIRCRAFT WAS ATTACHED TO THE TUG, PASSENGERS WERE ADVISED OF A BRAKING SYSTEM MALFUNCTION AND INFORMED THAT THE AIRCRAFT WOULD BE TOWED TO THE RAMP, RESULTING IN A SLIGHT DELAY TO ARRIVAL.

THE AIRCRAFT WAS TOWED TO THE RAMP WITHOUT FURTHER INCIDENT. NO INJURIES OCCURRED.

SHUT DOWN BOTH ENGINES TO PREVENT UNINTENDED MOVEMENT

RTK DATA INDICATES THAT THE SYSTEM REJECTED A-SIDE RTK CORRECTIONS APPROXIMATELY HALFWAY THROUGH THE MISSION AND OPERATED ON A COMPUTE B SOLUTION FOR THE REMAINDER OF FLIGHT.  POST-IMPACT DATA SHOWS THE A-SIDE RTK RESIDUAL DECREASING AND THE NAVIGATION SOLUTION REACQUIRING A VALID FIX DURING DOCKING. ANALYSIS SUGGESTS THE AIRCRAFT WAS OPERATING ON AN INCORRECT (FALSE) RTK FIX FOR A PORTION OF THE FLIGHT AND REACQUIRED A CORRECT FIX AT OR IMMEDIATELY AFTER DOCK CONTACT.  PRELIMINARY NAVIGATION ANALYSIS INDICATES THE EVENT WAS LIKELY DUE TO A FALSE GNSS/RTK POSITION SOLUTION AND IS NOT ATTRIBUTED TO EXTERNAL INTERFERENCE AFFECTING OTHER AIRCRAFT. DURING THE ENGINE OVERHAUL, UNDER THE DISASSEMBLY PROCESS, WE FOUND A MOUNTED EXTERNAL SPIN-ON OIL FILTER. HOWEVER, THE ENGINE STILL RETAINED ITS ORIGINAL INTERNAL MESH OIL FILTER. THE ORIGINAL FILTER CONTAINED A SIGNIFICANT AMOUNT OF OIL SLUDGE, DEPOSITS, AND METAL PARTICLES, WHILE THE SPIN-ON FILTER SHOWED NO CONTAMINATION.  THE CONCLUSION IS THAT THE MODIFICATION PERFORMED ON THIS ENGINE WAS INCORRECT. WHEN AN OIL FILTER ADAPTER IS INSTALLED, THE ORIGINAL MESH FILTER MUST BE REMOVED SO THAT ONLY THE SPIN-ON FILTER IS IN USE.  UNDER THESE CONDITIONS, MAINTENANCE PERSONNEL WOULD TYPICALLY INSPECT ONLY THE SPIN-ON FILTER AND NOT THE ORIGINAL INTERNAL FILTER. THIS CAN LEAD TO THE ORIGINAL FILTER BECOMING CLOGGED, CAUSING ENGINE OIL STARVATION AND RESULTING IN SEVERE ENGINE DAMAGE AS EVIDENCED BY THIS ENGINE AND THE AMOUNT OF DEBRIS FOUND IN THE ORIGINAL FILTER.

PITCH TRIM WHEEL COULD ONLY BE MOVED WITHIN A VERY SMALL RANGE.  MAINTENANCE INVESTIGATED AND FOUND THAT THE LH PITCH TRIM ACTUATOR WAS BOUND UP AND WOULD NOT ROTATE. THE ACTUATOR WAS REMOVED AND DISASSEMBLED IAW THE KODIAK 100 AMM CH. 2731.5.10 AND DAHER FIELD SERVICE INSTRUCTION FSI-184 PITCH TRIM TAB ACTUATOR MAINTENANCE.  THE RAMS AND RAM HOUSINGS WERE REMOVED AND WERE FOUND TO BE ADEQUATELY GREASED (GREASING WAS RECORDED A YEAR PRIOR) AND NOT THE CAUSE OF THE PROBLEM.  FSI-184 DOESN'T GIVE FURTHER DISASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS. HOWEVER, THE OTHER HALF OF THE ACTUATOR WAS DISASSEMBLED TO GIVE ACCESS TO THE GEARBOX. DESPITE SOME GREASE STILL REMAINING, THE DRIVE GEAR AND THE TWO DRIVEN GEARS FOR THE JACKSCREWS WERE HEAVILY CORRODED.  THE RUST IN THE GEAR TEETH WAS CAUSING THE ACTUATOR TO JAM.  THE OTHER OTHER ACTUATOR (RH) WAS DISASSEMBLED AND INSPECTED AND FOUND TO HAVE VERY LITTLE CORROSION.  IT WAS COMPLETELY GREASED ON THE INSIDE AND ON THE JACKSCREW THREADS AS DIRECTED BY FSI-184 ITCH TRIM TAB ACTUATOR MAINTENANCE AND REINSTALLED ON THE AIRCRAFT.  THE FAILED ACTUATOR WAS REPLACED WITH A NEW COMPONENT.  THIS IS A SAFETY OF FLIGHT ISSUE.  IT IS POSSIBLE FOR THE PITCH TRIM SYSTEM TO BE SOMEWHAT OPERATIONAL (BUT STIFFLY).  ONCE THE AIRCRAFT IS FLYING THE AIR LOADS ON THE TRIM TAB CAN RESIST AN INTERNALLY CORRODED ACTUATOR FROM TURNING COMPLETELY.  IF THE PILOT CHOOSES TO USE ELECTRIC TRIM AND NOT MANUALLY TRIM IMMEDIATELY AFTER TAKEOFF, HE/SHE MAY NOT NOTICE THAT THE TRIM IS NOT MOVING UNTIL THE AIRLOADS INCREASE TO THE POINT THAT THE PILOT HAS DIFFICULTY HOLDING THE ELEVATOR CONTROL.  EVEN THEN, DUE TO THE AIR LOADS, THE PITCH TRIM THAT MIGHT HAVE WORKED ON THE GROUND, NO LONGER IS MOVEABLE IN FLIGHT.  WE ARE AWARE OF A FATAL ACCIDENT WITH ANOTHER OPERATOR OVERSEAS THAT OUR ORGANIZATION INVESTIGATED AND FOUND THAT ONE OR BOTH OF THE TRIM ACTUATORS FAILING IN THIS WAY CONTRIBUTED TO THE ACCIDENT. IT WAS DUE TO THIS ACCIDENT THAT QUEST/DAHER ISSUED FSI-184 AND REVISED THE AMM TO INCLUDE A TEST TO DETERMINE SERVICEABILITY OF THE PITCH TRIM SYSTEM.  HOWEVER, WE FEEL THEY DID NOT GO FAR ENOUGH TO INCLUDE INSPECTION AND LUBRICATION OF THE INTERNAL GEARBOX.

UPON APPROACH INTO PAKU IT WAS IDENTIFIED BY THE FLIGHT MECHANIC ONBOARD THAT THE NR 2 SPINNER SEEMED OFF OF CENTER AND HAD MORE MOVEMENT DURING ROTATION THAN TYPICAL.  AFTER LANDING THE MECH INVESTIGATED FURTHER & FOUND WHAT APPEARED TO BE LOOSE SLEEVE NUT FASTENERS ON THE SPINNER.  WHEN THESE FASTENERS WERE TORQUED 4 OF THE 12 PULLED THROUGH THE GROMMETS COMPLETELY DUE TO WEAR IN THE GROMMETS. THE SPINNER WAS THEN REMOVED AND IT WAS FOUND THAT AN ADDITIONAL 2 GROMMETS WERE WORN RESULTING IN AN INABILITY OF THE SLEEVE NUTS TO BE ABLE TO SECURE THE SPINNER PROPERLY. ALSO WHEN THE SPINNER WAS REMOVED IT WAS FOUND THAT THE RUBBER RING IN THE NOSE CONE BULKHEAD OF THE SPINNER WAS NO LONGER BONDED AND FELL OUT. THE RUBBER RING WAS CUT IN SUCH A WAY TO MAKE IT APPEAR THAT IT HAD BEEN IN PLACE FOR ONLY HALF OF THE CIRCUMFERENCE WHICH WOULD ALLOW THE NOSE OF THE SPINNER TO NOT BE PROPERLY SUPPORTED AND THEREFORE ALLOW THE SPINNER MORE MOVEMENT THAN TYPICAL. IT IS BELIEVED THAT THIS MOVEMENT CAUSED ACCELERATED WEAR OF THE GROMMETS SO THAT ONCE IDENTIFIED 6 OF THE 12 FASTENERS WERE NO LONGER ABLE TO SECURE THE SPINNER PROPERLY.

DURING A REPOSITION FROM SIGNATURE TERMINAL ONE TO SIGNATURE TERMINAL TWO IN DAL, A STRONG OZONE LIKE ODOR WAS ENTERING THE CABIN. BOTH OF US IN THE COCKPIT IMMEDIATELY NOTICED  SMOKE/HAZE. FLIGHT ATTENDANT RUSHED FORWARD, AND SAID THE CABIN IS FILLING WITH SMOKE. UNAWARE OF WHAT WAS GENERATING THE SMOKE WE IMMEDIATELY TURNED OFF THE CABIN. ALMOST SIMULTANEOUSLY THE L PACK FAIL AMBER CAS MESSAGE APPEARED. AT THIS TIME WE WERE PULLING ONTO THE RAMP, AND WE IMMEDIATELY TAXIED IN AND SHUT DOWN AND EVACUATED THE PLANE FOR FRESH AIR.   WE RE-ENTERED THE PLANE AND RAN THE LEFT PACK FAIL, AMBER CHECKLIST. THE LEFT PACK FAILED AGAIN.   ON THE ARRIVAL INTO DALLAS, LOVE, BOTH MYSELF, AND MY COPILOT THOUGHT WE GOT A SMALL SCENT OF SMOKE OR A STRANGE SMELL, BUT IT WAS NOT STRONG ENOUGH TO RAISE ANY CONCERN. ALMOST LIKE A CAP GUN OR IZONE SMELL. PASSENGERS WERE ON BOARD AT THAT TIME, BUT WE HAD NO COMPLAINTS AND RECEIVED PRAISES FOR OUR FLIGHT.   REMOVED THE ACM.  NSTALLED CUSTOMER SUPPLIED REPAIRED ACM. OPERATED THE APU FOR TWO HOURS, NO STRONG OZONE-LIKE ODOR DETECTED IN THE CABIN AND NO SMOKE OR HAZE OBSERVED. OPS CHECKS SATISFACTORY PER AMM 21-52-00.

IN CRUISE AT FL410, WE GOT A "AUTO PRES FAIL"  EICAS MESSAGE. IMMEDIATELY STARTED A DECENT TO A LOWER ALTITUDE AND RAN CHECKLIST BUT THE CABIN PRESSURE WOULD NOT RESPOND TO MANUAL INPUTS. THE CABIN WAS CLIMBING AT  ABOUT 4400FPM AT THIS POINT SO WE WENT ON O2 & DID AN EMERGENCY DECENT TO 10,000'. DURING A SOLO CROSS-COUNTRY FLIGHT, THE PILOT EXPERIENCED A SUDDEN ENG MALFUNCTION WHILE CRUISING AT APPROX 4,500 FT MSL NEAR KCSQ. THE ENGINE BEGAN OPERATING EXTREMELY ROUGH, ACCOMPANIED BY A FLASHING LANE A WARNING INDICATION & MULTIPLE INSTRUMENT DISPLAY FAILURES. SHORTLY AFTER, ENGINE OIL PRESSURE RAPIDLY DECREASED, FOLLOWED BY A COMPLETE LOSS OF ENG POWER DUE TO ENG SEIZURE.  THE PILOT SECURED THE ENG & CONDUCTED A SUCCESSFUL EMERGENCY LANDING IN AN AGRICULTURAL FIELD AFTER DETERMINING THAT KCSQ COULD NOT BE REACHED. THE PILOT WAS UNINJURED, AND NO SUBSTANTIAL AIRFRAME DAMAGE WAS OBSERVED DURING THE LANDING.  FOLLOWING THE INCIDENT, A SIGNIFICANT AMOUNT OF ENGINE OIL WAS FOUND COVERING THE LOWER COWLING AND NOSE LANDING GEAR AREA, INDICATING A SUBSTANTIAL LOSS OF ENGINE OIL DURING FLIGHT. SUBSEQUENT INSPECTION OF THE ENGINE REVEALED MULTIPLE CRACKS IN THE ENGINE CRANKCASE/BODY. THE ENGINE REMAINED SEIZED AND COULD NOT BE RESTARTED. NO DISCREPANCIES NOTED. THE ENGINE/AIRCRAFT IS CONSIDERED OUT OF SERVICE UNTIL THE OIL SAMPLE RESULTS HAVE BEEN RECEIVED AND EVALUATED BY P&W.

DURING CLIMB OUT EN ROUTE FROM HOU TO DAL, PASSING APPROXIMATELY FL200, THE CREW EXPERIENCED A SUDDEN AND MAJOR MECHANICAL FAILURE OF THE #2 ENGINE. THIS WAS INDICATED BY AN EICAS MESSAGE, ACCOMPANIED BY A RAPID CASCADE OF SECONDARY MASTER CAUTIONS, INCLUDING A LOSS OF GENERATORS, ICING CONDITION ALERTS, AND AN UNCOMMANDED RISE IN CABIN PRESSURE.  THE CREW IMMEDIATELY FOCUSED ON BASIC AIRCRAFT CONTROL AND STABILIZED THE AIRCRAFT. I CROSS-CHECKED THE EICAS INDICATIONS WITH PRIMARY ENGINE INSTRUMENTS. THE #2 ENGINE EXHIBITED ZERO ROTATION N2, AND SEVERE VIBRATION INDICATIONS PRIOR TO SPOOL-DOWN, CONFIRMING A CATASTROPHIC MECHANICAL FAILURE RATHER THAN A SIMPLE FLAMEOUT.  DUE TO THE SECONDARY INDICATIONS (CABIN PRESSURE RISING AND ICING CONDITIONS), THE WORKLOAD IN THE COCKPIT WAS EXTREMELY HIGH. I INITIATED A CONTROLLED DESCENT TO 12,000 FEET TO ADDRESS THE PRESSURIZATION ISSUE, PROVIDE A WARMER/DENSER AIR MASS, AND CLEAR THE IMMEDIATE ICING THREAT WHILE THE FIRST OFFICER EXECUTED THE APPROPRIATE QRH CHECKLISTS (ENGINE OUT).   IMMEDIATELY FOLLOWING THE ENGINE FAILURE AND EICAS CASCADE, I NOTIFIED ATC OF OUR OPERATIONAL STATUS (LOSS OF ENGINE #2 AND SECONDARY SYSTEMS ISSUES). ATC IMMEDIATELY PROVIDED PRIORITY HANDLING, CLEARING THE AIRSPACE AHEAD OF US AND GRANTING US DIRECT ROUTING. BECAUSE ATC HAD ALREADY SEAMLESSLY INTEGRATED US INTO A PRIORITY HANDLING FLOW TOWARD THE DALLAS AREA, AND BECAUSE THE AIRCRAFT WAS STABILIZED AT 12,000 FEET, DIVERTING ABRUPTLY INTO A CLOSER AIRPORT WOULD HAVE DISRUPTED THIS STABLE ATC FLOW, FORCED A RAPID DESCENT, AND INCREASED CREW WORKLOAD DURING CRITICAL CHECKLIST EXECUTION.   AFTER STABILIZING THE AIRCRAFT AT 12,000 FEET AND SECURING THE #2 ENGINE, I EVALUATED THE BEST COURSE OF ACTION. WHILE COLLEGE STATION (CLL) WAS GEOGRAPHICALLY CLOSER, I DETERMINED IT WAS NOT THE SAFEST SUITABLE AIRPORT.   TIME AND COCKPIT WORKLOAD: RUSHING AN IMMEDIATE APPROACH INTO CLL WOULD HAVE FORCED THE CREW TO CONDUCT CRITICAL EMERGENCY CHECKLISTS WHILE SIMULTANEOUSLY MANEUVERING FOR A SHORT-RANGE ARRIVAL. THIS WOULD HAVE SEVERELY DEGRADED OUR SITUATIONAL AWARENESS AND INCREASED THE RISK OF A RUSHED, UNSTABILIZED APPROACH.  AIRPORT CAPABILITY & WEATHER: DALLAS LOVE FIELD (DAL) OFFERED SUPERIOR RUNWAY LENGTHS, FAVORABLE WEATHER, MAXIMUM ARFF (EMERGENCY SERVICES) CAPABILITY, AND A FAMILIAR ATC ENVIRONMENT.  SINGLE-ENGINE PERFORMANCE IN ICING: GIVEN THAT WE HAD ENCOUNTERED ICING CONDITIONS, MAXIMIZING OUR OPERATIONAL SAFETY MARGIN BY TRANSITIONING TO A HIGH-CAPABILITY ENVIRONMENT (DAL) WAS DEEMED SAFER THAN ATTEMPTING AN IMMEDIATE PENETRATION OF WEATHER INTO A LOWER-CAPABILITY FIELD WITH SINGLE-ENGINE ANTI-ICE LOADS.  . APPROACH AND LANDING.  BY ELECTING TO CONTINUE TO DAL, THE CREW HAD SUFFICIENT TIME TO METHODICALLY SECURE THE FAILED ENGINE, STABILIZE THE CABIN PRESSURE, CONFIGURE THE ELECTRICAL SYSTEM, AND BRIEF THE PASSENGERS AND FLIGHT ATTENDANTS. WE WERE CLEARED FOR AND EXECUTED THE ILS RUNWAY 13L APPROACH INTO DAL. UTILIZING A PRECISION ILS APPROACH ALLOWED US TO MAINTAIN A LOW-WORKLOAD, HIGHLY STABILIZED ENVIRONMENT UTILIZING THE AUTOPILOT. ATC WAS FULLY COORDINATED, EMERGENCY EQUIPMENT WAS STAGED, AND A STABLE, SINGLE-ENGINE PRECISION LANDING WAS EXECUTED WITHOUT FURTHER INCIDENT. THE DECISION TO CONTINUE TO DAL WAS MADE ENTIRELY IN THE INTEREST OF SAFETY, PRIORITIZING WORKLOAD MANAGEMENT, ASSET AVAILABILITY, AND A STABILIZED APPROACH OVER A RUSHED, HIGH-RISK DIVERSION. DURING CLIMB IN HEADING MODE AND WHILE DEVIATING FOR WEATHER, ATC ISSUED A DIRECT-TO DUCEN CLEARANCE ON THE AGERS1 SID. DURING THIS PHASE, THE CREW OBSERVED THAT FMS 1 WAS NOT FUNCTIONING PROPERLY. AT THAT TIME, CONTROL OF THE AIRCRAFT WAS TRANSFERRED TO THE FIRST OFFICER, WHOSE FMS 2 WAS OPERATING NORMALLY, IN ORDER TO CONTINUE NAVIGATION DIRECT TO DUCEN. THE PIC ASSUMED COMMUNICATIONS WITH ATC AND BEGAN TROUBLESHOOTING FMS 1.  SUBSEQUENTLY, ATC CLEARED THE AIRCRAFT TO CLIMB TO FL310. SHORTLY THEREAFTER, THE FIRST OFFICER’S PFD FAILED, IMMEDIATELY FOLLOWED BY THE DETECTION OF AN ELECTRICAL ODOR IN THE COCKPIT.  THE PIC IMMEDIATELY ASSUMED CONTROL OF THE AIRCRAFT, DECLARED AN EMERGENCY WITH ATC FOR SMOKE/FUMES IN THE COCKPIT, AND INITIATED AN EMERGENCY DESCENT TO THE ASSIGNED ALTITUDE OF 11,000 FEET. THE FIRST OFFICER WAS DIRECTED TO BEGIN THE “SMOKE AND FUMES” EMERGENCY CHECKLIST.  AT NO TIME WAS VISIBLE SMOKE OBSERVED IN THE COCKPIT OR CABIN. THE PASSENGERS WERE PROMPTLY INFORMED BY THE PILOT MONITORING THAT A MAINTENANCE-RELATED ISSUE HAD OCCURRED AND WERE INSTRUCTED TO REMAIN SEATED WITH SEATBELTS FASTENED.  BOTH PILOTS DONNED OXYGEN MASKS AND CONTINUED WITH THE APPROPRIATE CHECKLIST PROCEDURES WHILE CONDUCTING THE EMERGENCY DESCENT. THE PIC REQUESTED RADAR VECTORS BACK TO KFLL.  THE “SMOKE AND FUMES IN THE COCKPIT” CHECKLIST WAS COMPLETED TO THE FIRST DECISION POINT, AT WHICH TIME THE CREW DETERMINED THAT THE ODOR HAD DISSIPATED. ATC PROVIDED VECTORS AND ALTITUDE ASSIGNMENTS FOR THE RETURN TO KFLL.  THE PIC CONTINUED AIRCRAFT CONTROL WHILE THE FIRST OFFICER CONFIGURED THE COCKPIT FOR AN ILS APPROACH TO RUNWAY 10L. ALL APPLICABLE DESCENT, APPROACH, AND BEFORE-LANDING CHECKLISTS WERE COMPLETED. THE AIRCRAFT LANDED SAFELY ON RUNWAY 10L AND TAXIED VIA TAXIWAYS B, C4, C, AND E TO SIGNATURE AVIATION.  THE PIC DETERMINED THAT NO ADDITIONAL EMERGENCY SERVICES WERE REQUIRED UPON ARRIVAL. THE AIRCRAFT WAS SHUT DOWN AND SECURED BY THE CREW. THE FIRST OFFICER DE-POWERED THE AIRCRAFT, AND THE PIC SUBSEQUENTLY OPENED THE CABIN DOOR FOR THE SEVEN PASSENGERS. ONE PASSENGER BRIEFLY RECEIVED MEDICAL ATTENTION FROM AIRPORT EMERGENCY PERSONNEL AND WAS ABLE TO DEPART THE AIRPORT UNDER THEIR OWN POWER.

ABOUT 1.25 SECONDS LATER, THE SAME PROPELLER EXPERIENCED A SECOND IMPACT AND STOPPED COMPLETELY, LIKELY CAUSING THE BOOM ARM (FWD RIGHT) TO FRACTURE AND THE MOTOR ASSEMBLY TO SEPARATE FROM THE AIRCRAFT.  FOLLOWING THE FAILURE, THE AIRCRAFT EXPERIENCED SIGNIFICANT PITCH AND YAW MOVEMENT DUE TO THE LOSS OF PROPULSION AND IMBALANCE FROM THE DAMAGED ROTOR SYSTEM. DATA ALSO SHOWED SUSTAINED VIBRATION AFTER THE INITIAL IMPACT, INDICATING PROPELLER DAMAGE OCCURRED BEFORE THE BOOM SEPARATED.  THE AIRCRAFT CONTINUED FLIGHT WITH DEGRADED PERFORMANCE AND LATER RECOVERED SAFELY. AIRCRAFT: ZIPLINE, P2ZIP

PROBLEM: A ZIP DRONE RETURNED TO DOCK AT PEA RIDGE WITH A BROKEN PROPELLER AND BOOM ARM AFTER A LOUD POPPING NOISE WAS HEARD ON APPROACH.  IMPACT: ONE ZIP AT PEA RIDGE SUFFERED A BROKEN PROPELLER AND BOOM ARM (AFT LEFT). THERE HAVE BEEN NO INJURIES, AND ALL PERSONNEL ARE SAFE. OPERATIONS WERE BRIEFLY INTERRUPTED FOR THE AFFECTED VEHICLE, BUT THERE IS NO INDICATION OF BROADER SERVICE DISRUPTION. CAUSES: FIELD EVIDENCE AND TELEMETRY DATA INDICATE THE ZIP DRONE MOST LIKELY STRUCK A BIRD DURING ITS RETURN FLIGHT, LEADING TO THE PROPELLER BREAKING AND SUBSEQUENT BOOM ARM FAILURE. ALL PHYSICAL PIECES WERE RECOVERED, AND POSSIBLE BLOOD ON THE BLADE SUPPORTS THIS CONCLUSION. HOWEVER, NO BIRD REMAINS HAVE BEEN FOUND, AND ENGINEERING HAS NOTED THAT IT'S NOT POSSIBLE TO DETERMINE WITH CERTAINTY IF THE FAILURE WAS CAUSED BY A STRIKE OR PROP IMBALANCE. OPERATOR HAS EXPERIENCED A RECURRING L BLEED AIR LEAK EICAS MESSAGE ACROSS A FLEET OF FIVE LEARJET 45XR AIRCRAFT EQUIPPED WITH HONEYWELL TFE731-20BR ENGINES. THE DISCREPANCY IS INTERMITTENT AND HAS NOT BEEN REPRODUCIBLE DURING GROUND TROUBLESHOOTING, MAKING ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFICATION DIFFICULT.  FOR THIS EVENT, THE DISCREPANCY OCCURRED OVER A PERIOD OF SEVERAL WEEKS. INITIAL REPORTS INDICATED THE L BLEED AIR LEAK MESSAGE WOULD ILLUMINATE INTERMITTENTLY DURING FLIGHT AND EXTINGUISH WITHOUT MAINTENANCE INTERVENTION. IN ONE OCCURRENCE, THE MESSAGE APPEARED DURING DESCENT PASSING APPROXIMATELY FL120. ADVANCING THE THRUST LEVERS CAUSED THE MESSAGE TO EXTINGUISH AND IT DID NOT REOCCUR DURING THE REMAINDER OF THE FLIGHT. MAINTENANCE ACCOMPLISHED EXTENSIVE TROUBLESHOOTING OF THE BLEED AIR LEAK DETECTION SYSTEM AND ASSOCIATED DUCTING. INSPECTIONS INCLUDED BLEED AIR PLUMBING, SENSING LINES, CONNECTORS, THERMAL BLANKETS, JOINTS, AND DUCT ASSEMBLIES THROUGHOUT THE BAGGAGE COMPARTMENT, BELLY, AND ENGINE PYLON AREAS. MULTIPLE CORRECTIVE ACTIONS WERE PERFORMED,  INSPECTION, CLEANING, AND RESEATING OF BLEED AIR LEAK DETECTOR CONNECTORS.  REPLACEMENT OF LP DUCT SLIP-JOINT SEALS ADJACENT TO LEAK DETECTION SENSING LINES. REPLACEMENT OF HP DUCT SEALS ADJACENT TO LEAK DETECTION SENSING LINES. REPLACEMENT OF RH LP DUCT ASSEMBLY SEALS PER LEARJET TECHNICAL SUPPORT RECOMMENDATION. REPLACEMENT OF LH ECS SHUTOFF VALVE WITH A SERVICEABLE UNIT. REPLACEMENT OF ECS CONTROLLER. INSPECTION AND TIGHTENING OF BLEED AIR LEAK DETECTION SENSING LINES. FOLLOWING EACH MAINTENANCE ACTION, GROUND RUNS AT VARYING POWER SETTINGS WERE SATISFACTORY. MULTIPLE MAINTENANCE CHECK FLIGHTS WERE CONDUCTED ATTEMPTING TO DUPLICATE THE REPORTED CONDITIONS. MOST CHECK FLIGHTS WERE SATISFACTORY AND THE AIRCRAFT WAS REPEATEDLY RETURNED TO SERVICE. HOWEVER, THE DISCREPANCY CONTINUED TO RECUR DURING SUBSEQUENT REVENUE FLIGHTS, INCLUDING BOTH CLIMB AND CRUISE PHASES OF FLIGHT. IN ONE INSTANCE, THE DISCREPANCY RETURNED APPROXIMATELY TWO DAYS AFTER MAINTENANCE ACTION; IN ANOTHER, IT OCCURRED DURING CLIMB THROUGH APPROXIMATELY 8,000 FEET MSL.  THROUGHOUT THE TROUBLESHOOTING PROCESS, NO ACTUAL BLEED AIR LEAK OR OVERHEAT CONDITION COULD BE POSITIVELY IDENTIFIED. THE DISCREPANCY REMAINS INTERMITTENT AND FLIGHT-CONDITION DEPENDENT. THE INABILITY TO REPRODUCE THE EVENT ON THE GROUND HAS SIGNIFICANTLY COMPLICATED TROUBLESHOOTING EFFORTS AND RESULTED IN REPEATED AIRCRAFT DOWNTIME.

DURING CRUISE FLIGHT, CABIN FUMES WERE DETECTED, FOLLOWED BY VISIBLE SMOKE. THE FLIGHT CREW EXECUTED THE EMERGENCY PROCEDURES AND CHECKLISTS, WHICH INCLUDED SHUTTING DOWN ALL NON-ESSENTIAL SYSTEMS. TURNING OFF THE FOOT HEATER IMMEDIATELY AFTER DETECTING THE FUMES PREVENTED THEM FROM WORSENING. SHORTLY THEREAFTER, THE SMOKE SUBSIDED AND BEGAN TO DISSIPATE. THE REMAINING DESCENT, APPROACH, LANDING, AND TAXI WERE UNEVENTFUL. A POST-FLIGHT MAINTENANCE INSPECTION DETERMINED THAT THE FOOT HEATER WIRING AT THE CONNECTOR HAD OVERHEATED, MELTING THE PLASTIC CONNECTION COATING. AIRCRAFT CURRENTLY OOS AWT PARTS.

AIRCRAFT WAS GROUNDED. AN EMERGENCY WAS DECLARED AND THE AIRCRAFT RETURNED TO CLT. THE CAPTAIN REPORTED ON ROTATION THAT THE AC WAS SLUGGISH AND SLOW TO ACCELERATE. DURING CLIMBOUT, THE AIRCRAFT FLIGHT DIRECTOR WAS PITCHING INTO VLS AND CONFIRMED SPEED WAS MANAGED, PM CONFIRMED IT WAS MANAGED, AND THE FMA READ MANAGED. THE SPEED BUG WAS WHERE IT SHOULD HAVE BEEN, BUT THE FLIGHT DIRECTOR WAS PITCHING UP A SLOWING INTO THE VLS. CAPT SELECTED SPEED AND ROLLED IT UP TO 250 KTS. AC WAS STILL SLOW TO RESPOND AND CAPT TURNED OFF ATS WITH AUTO THRUST PB AND MANUALLY TOOK CONTROL, THE FLIGHT CREW INITIALLY HAD TO PUSH THE TLA ABOVE THE CLIMB DETENT WHEN AIRCRAFT TRENDED SLOW AS THE AIRCRAFT CLIMBED. ONCE LEVEL AT 6000 MSL THE FLIGHT CREW ATTEMPTED TO RE-ESTABLISH THE AUTO THRUST. AFTER RESELECTING ATH PB ON AND PLACING TLAS INTO CLIMB DETENT, AND MANAGING SPEED, THE SPEED ACCELERATED RAPIDLY ABOVE 250. CAPT USED ATH TLA BELOW THE CLIMB DETENT TO MAINTAIN SPEED. PF CYCLED THE FD SWITCHED AND ATH PB AGAIN. SPEED REMAINED STABLE AFTER PLACING THE ATH TLAS BACK INTO THE CLIMB DETENT. CAPT PUSHED IT PAST THE CLB NOTCH, AND BACK INTO FLX. CAPT THEN SELECTED AUTOPILOT. AIRCRAFT REMAINED STABLE. THE AIRCRAFT LANDED SAFELY AT CLT WITHOUT FURTHER INCIDENT. MAINTENANCE REPLACED FAC2 PER AMM 22-66-34 (AALA202606089397) AND THE FCU PER AMM 22-81-12 (AALA202606085312). A SATISFACTORY OPERATIONAL CHECK WAS ACCOMPLISHED.

THIS IS AN AMPHIBIAN DESIGN WITH THE ENG MOUNTED ABOVE THE WING.  THE SEAMAX M22 HAS HAD ENGINE FIRES. THERE ARE A TOTAL OF 5 FUEL VENT LINES THAT EXHAUST INTO THE ENGINE NACELLE. 2 COME FROM THE RIGHT WING TANK, 2 COME FROM THE LEFT WING TANK, AND 1 COMES FROM THE HEADER TANK. USING UV TRACER DYE,  DETERMINED THAT NOT ONLY IS FUEL VAPOR EXHAUSTS IN TO THE NACELLE, BUT UNDER CERTAIN CIRCUMSTANCES, RAW FUEL WILL ENTER THE ENGINE NACELLE VIA THE HEADER TANK VENT LINE.  I'VE SEEN NO EVIDENCE OF THE RIGHT OR LEFT TANK VENTS EJECTING RAW FUEL, BUT DEFINITELY THE HEADER TANK LINE WILL EJECT RAW FUEL.  THE ISSUE OCCURS WHEN THE TANKS ARE FULL, ROUGH WATER TAKEOFFS, AS WELL AS STEEP TURNS.  INTERESTINGLY, THE OIL TANK VENT LINE EXHAUSTS OUTSIDE OF THE NACELLE.

ENROUTE TO A DIP SITE FOR ANOTHER BUCKET OF WATER THE PILOT SMELLED ELECTRICAL SMOKE IN THE CABIN OF THE AIRCRAFT. ODOR WAS IMMEDIATELY FOLLOWED BY SMOKE COMING FROM UNDER THE CENTER CONSOLE WHICH FILLED THE HELICOPTER CABIN. THE PILOT CALLED IN A MAYDAY OVER THE RADIO AND BEGAN FLYING TO AN OPEN FIELD NORTHWEST OF BUCKWITH RESERVOIR TO MAKE AN EMERGENCY LANDING. AIR ATTACK HALTED AIR OPERATIONS AND FOLLOWED THE AIRCRAFT TO THE EMERGENCY LANDING SITE. ANOTHER HELICOPTER AND LARGE AIR TANKER ON THE INCIDENT ALSO FOLLOWED TO ENSURE THEY COULD PROVIDE HELP IF NEEDED. THE PILOT SHUT OFF THE THREE BATTERY SWITCHES ENROUTE TO THE LANDING SITE WHICH IMMEDIATELY CAUSED THE SMOKE TO SUBSIDE. WHILE THIS WAS OCCURRING AIR ATTACK INFORMED THE GROUND RESOURCES AND THE MANAGER OF THE HELICOPTER OVER THE VHF AIR TO GROUND INCIDENT FREQUENCY. THE CREW CAPTAIN THAT WAS MANAGING ONE OF THE DIP SITES MADE HIS WAY TO THE EMERGENCY LANDING SITE. NOTIFICATIONS WERE MADE FOLLOWING THE MISHAP RESPONSE PLAN AND ALL NECESSARY PERSONNEL WERE INFORMED OF THE UNFOLDING SITUATION. THE PILOT WAS ABLE TO SAFELY PUT THE AIRCRAFT ON THE GROUND WITH NO INJURY OR FURTHER DAMAGE TO THE AIRCRAFT. THE DISTRICT CHIEF FOR THE AREA ARRIVED AT THE EMERGENCY LANDING SITE FIRST AND CONFIRMED THE LATITUDE AND LONGITUDE AS WELL AS CONFIRMED THAT THE PILOT WAS OKAY. NO FURTHER DAMAGE TO THE AIRCRAFT WAS CAUSED WHILE LANDING. THE MANAGER WAS ALSO ABLE TO REACH THE PILOT VIA CELL PHONE AND CONFIRMED THAT THE PILOT WAS OKAY. THE CREW CAPTAIN ARRIVED AT THE EMERGENCY LANDING SITE SHORTLY AFTER AND ENSURED THAT THE MECHANIC WAS ENROUTE. THIS HAS HAPPENED TO ME ON AT LEAST TWO DIFFERENT PC12S. MY THEORY IS THAT WATER ENTERS THE PITOT SYSTEM AND FREEZES BEFORE IT CAN DRAIN OUT, AS THE SYSTEM RECOVERS WHEN DESCENDING THROUGH THE FREEZING LEVEL.

RIGHT SIDE PITOT LINE BECAME BLOCKED INFLIGHT AFTER EXTENDED OPERATION IN AN AREA OF VISIBLE MOISTURE AT BELOW-FREEZING TEMPERATURE. ALL PROBE HEATS WERE ON AND FUNCTIONAL AT THE TIME AND FOR THE ENTIRE DURATION OF FLIGHT PRIOR TO THE LINE BLOCKAGE. AIRSPEED ON THE RIGHT-SIDE PFD AND STANDBY INSTRUMENT SLOWLY DECREASED, WHICH CAUSED AN IAS MISCOMPARE ANNUNCIATOR. I STARTED A DESCENT FOR WEATHER AND THE AIRSPEED ON THE RIGHT-SIDE PITOT LINE (RIGHT PFD AND STANDBY) RAPIDLY DECREASED TO ZERO BEFORE AN IAS RED ANNUNCIATOR APPEARED. PRIOR TO THIS, I SWITCHED THE RIGHT-SIDE PFD TO ADAHRS 1, WHICH KEPT THE AUTOPILOT RUNNING FOR A WHILE UNTIL THE MISCOMPARE BECAME TOO GREAT AND THE AUTOPILOT DISCONNECTED. AUTOPILOT WOULDN'T REENGAGE UNTIL I PULLED THE ADAHARS CH 2 CIRCUIT BREAKER. AFTER DESCENDING OUT OF VISIBLE MOISTURE, THE RIGHT-SIDE AIRSPEED RAPIDLY RETURNED, AS SEEN ON THE STANDBY INSTRUMENT, AND WHEN THE ADAHRS 2 BREAKER WAS RESET, ALL SYSTEMS ON INDEPENDENT ADAHRS UNITS RETURNED TO NORMAL WITH NO FURTHER ISSUES.

THE PIC THEN SELECTED IGN FOR BOTH ENGINES USING THE IGNITION SELECTOR AS WE INITIATED A DESCENT AND UPON OBSERVING ITT HAD INCREASED ON NR 1 ENG TO 922C WE ELECTED TO SHUT DOWN NR 1 ENG IAW THE APPLICABLE PROCEDURES. DIVERTED TO KLNK,  CONTINUED DESCENDING TO FL240 & COMPLETED THE ENG NR 1 RESTART PROCEDURE USING THE ABNORMAL PROCEDURES CHECKLIST. THE RESTART WAS SUCCESSFUL. FOLLOWING STARTER CUTOUT, MONITORED ENGINE NR 1 VIBRATION AND ITT, BOTH OF WHICH WERE INITIALLY WITHIN NORMAL OPERATING LIMITS. THE ENGINE NR 1 VIBRATION INDICATION INCREASED FROM APPROXIMATELY 0.12 AND CONTINUED TO RISE STEADILY TO 0.80 AT WHICH POINT, ELECTED TO SHUTDOWN & SECURE ENG NR 1 A SECOND TIME. DECLARED AN EMERGENCY & CONTINUED TO KLNK WHERE THERE WAS MAINT ON THE FIELD.  ARCFT LANDED WITHOUT FURTHER INCIDENT. THERE WERE 5 SOULS ON BOARD AND APPROXIMATELY 90 MINUTES OF FUEL REMAINING AT LANDING.

DURING DISAS-SEMBLY, AN INCORRECTLY INSTALLED HIGH-PRESSURE COMPRESSOR (HPC) INLET GUIDE VANE (IGV) WAS IDENTIFIED ON ENGINE.  SPECIFICALLY IT WAS DISCOVERED AT THE FAN HUB FRAME EXPOSURE THAT IGV POSITION 19 WAS INSTALLED WITH ITS LEADING AND TRAILING EDGES ORIENTED 180° OPPOSITE TO THOSE OF THE OTHER IGVS IN THE FAN BOOSTER COMPRESSOR (FBC) MODULE.  FOR VARIABLE HPC STATOR VANES THIS CONDITION WOULD BE CLASSIFIED AS OFF-SCHEDULE VANE (VSV) OPERATION, AS OUT-LINED IN EM 72-00-00 INSPECTION 002, SUBTASK 72-00-00-220-089 WHILE THIS CONDITION FOR IGVS IS NOT DESCRIBED. ACCORDING TO THE REFERENCED SUBTASK, THE BLADES OF ONE STAGE FORWARD AND TWO STAGES AFT MUST BE SCRAPPED. PER RECENT OEM INQUIRIES IGV MISORIENTATION DOES NOT REQUIRE THE FORWARD (LPC STAGE) TO BE SCRAPPED.  THE AFFECTED ENGINE HAD PREVIOUSLY UNDERGONE MAINTENANCE.  INITIATED AN INTERNAL INVESTIGATION TO DETERMINE THE ROOT CAUSE AND IMPLEMENT APPROPRIATE CORRECTION.  A REVIEW OF MAINTENANCE RECORDS INDICATED THAT SIMILAR WORK WAS PERFORMED ON A TOTAL OF 29 ENGINES (2 ENGINES UNDER N-REGISTRATION ESN: 901500 AND 906440 ). ALL OF THESE ENGINES UNDERWENT MAINTENANCE ON THE FBC MODULE OR PROPULSOR, WHICH INCLUDED THE REPLACEMENT OF THE VSV PIN BUSHINGS. THIS WORK SCOPE NECESSITATES THE REMOVAL OF EACH INDIVIDUAL IGV LEVER ARM, ALLOWING THE IGVS TO MOVE FREELY ALONG THEIR AXES. CONSEQUENTLY, THE CHANGE IN ORIENTATION MAY GO UNDETECTED PRIOR TO THE REINSTALLATION OF THE LEVER ARM, POTENTIAL-LY LEADING TO MISALIGNMENT. BASED ON THE MAINTENANCE RECORDS, IT CANNOT BE RULED OUT THAT INDIVIDUAL IGVS RE-MAINED IN INCORRECTLY INSTALLED POSITION IN THE POTENTIALLY AFFECTED ENGINE POPULATION.  REACHED OUT TO THE ORIGINAL EQUIPMENT MANUFACTURER (OEM) FOR TECHNICAL SUPPORT. THE OEM HAS STATED THAT AN INSPECTION SHALL TAKE PLACE ON THE NEXT OPPORTUNITY AND THE ENGINE CANNOT CONTINUE TO OPERATE AFTER DETECTION OF AN INCORRECTLY INSTALLED IGV.  IN THE EVENT THAT AN INCORRECTLY INSTALLED IGV IS IDENTIFIED, THE AFFECTED HARDWARE MIGHT BE MANAGED IN ACCORD-ANCE WITH EM 72-00-00 INSPECTION 002, SUBTASK 72-00-00-220-089. ACCORDING TO THIS SUBTASK, THE LPC STAGE 5, HPC BLISK STAGE 1, AND HPC BLADES STAGE 2 SHALL BE REPLACED BEFORE ANY FURTHER OPERATION CAN TAKE PLACE.  AS OUTLINED IN GE CASE #02094147 FOR ESN 906603, #02028374 FOR ESN 906607 (BOTH CASES INITIATED BY MTU-H), AND #02382854-B FOR ESN 907411 (INITIATED BY HAECO), ONLY THE HPC BLISK STAGE 1 AND HPC BLADES STAGE 2, AS WELL AS THE IMPACTED IGVS WITH LEVER ARMS AND ASSOCIATED HARDWARE, ALONG WITH BOTH ADJACENT IGVS (RIGHT AND LEFT) OF THE REVERSED IGV WITH LEVER ARMS AND ASSOCIATED HARDWARE, MUST BE DISCARDED REGARDLESS OF THEIR VISUAL CONDITION.   CONTINUE TO COLLABORATE WITH THE OEM IN THIS MATTER.

TO IDENTIFY THE SUSPECTED POPULATION, MTU-H REVIEWED ALL SHOP VISITS INVOLVING WORK SCOPES THAT REQUIRED REMOVAL AND REINSTALLATION OF IGV LEVER ARMS WITHOUT ACCESS TO THE IGVS. THE POPULATION WAS SUBSEQUENTLY NARROWED BY EXCLUDING ENGINES FOR WHICH THE FAN HUB FRAME (FHF) WAS EXPOSED AT MODULE LEVEL, SUCH AS DURING HPC MODULE REMOVAL, AS THE IGVS ARE VISIBLE AND CAN BE VISUALLY INSPECTED AFTER LEVER ARM INSTALLATION. IN ADDITION, ENGINES THAT UNDERWENT A SUBSEQUENT SHOP VISIT WITH THE FHF EXPOSED WERE ALSO EXCLUDED FROM THE SUSPECTED POPULATION. THE REMAINING ENGINES WERE THEREFORE CLASSIFIED AS POTENTIALLY AFFECTED. IT SHOULD BE NOTED THAT WORK SCOPES PROVIDING ACCESS TO THE IGVS INCLUDE SEVERAL QUALITY GATES DURING ASSEMBLY THAT ARE INTENDED TO IDENTIFY ANY LEVER ARM MISORIENTATION THROUGH VISUAL INSPECTION. FURTHERMORE, THE APPLICABLE TASK CARDS REQUIRE A VERIFICATION OF THE IGV POSITIONS FOLLOWING LEVER ARM INSTALLATION TO PREVENT INCORRECT ORIENTATION. THE IDENTIFIED POTENTIALLY AFFECTED CUSTOMERS AND RELEVANT AUTHORITIES WERE SUBSEQUENTLY  INFORMED.  ALL POTENTIALLY AFFECTED ENGINES IN SHOP WERE CHECKED PRIOR SHIPMENT. THE INTERNAL ASSEMBLY AND INSPECTION PROCEDURES WERE CHECKED AND REVISED TO IMPLEMENT AN ADDITIONAL BORESCOPE INSPECTION (BSI) AFTER ENGINE ASSEMBLY FOR ENGINES WITHOUT ACCESS TO THE IGVS TO DETERMINE THE CORRECT ORIENTATION OF ALL IGVS PRIOR TO ENGINE TESTING. A LESSONS LEARNED / QUALITY ALERT WAS DISTRIBUTED TO THE ENGINE AND MODULE ASSEMBLY SHOP STAFF TO RAISE AWARENESS ABOUT THIS TOPIC.  FOR VARIABLE HPC STATOR VANES THIS CONDITION WOULD BE CLASSIFIED AS OFF-SCHEDULE VANE (VSV) OPERATION, AS OUTLINED IN ESM 72-00-00 INSPECTION 002, SUBTASK 72-00-00-220-089 WHILE THIS CONDITION FOR IGVS IS NOT DESCRIBED. ACCORDING TO THE REFERENCED SUBTASK, THE BLADES OF ONE STAGE FORWARD AND TWO STAGES AFT MUST BE SCRAPPED. PER RECENT OEM INQUIRIES IGV MISORIENTATION DOES NOT REQUIRE THE FORWARD (LPC STAGE) TO BE SCRAPPED (SEE ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS).  A REVIEW OF MAINTENANCE RECORDS INDICATED, THAT SIMILAR WORK WAS PERFORMED ON MULTIPLE ENGINES. ALL OF THESE ENGINES UNDERWENT MAINTENANCE ON THE FBC MODULE OR ENGINE/PROPULSOR.  THIS WORKSCOPE INCLUDED THE REMOVAL OF IGV LEVER ARMS, ALLOWING THE IGVS TO MOVE FREELY AROUND THEIR INDIVIDUAL RADIAL AXES. CONSEQUENTLY, THE CHANGE IN ORIENTATION MAY GO UNDETECTED PRIOR TO THE REINSTALLATION OF THE LEVER ARM, POTENTIALLY LEADING TO MISALIGNMENT. THE ORIENTATION OF AN IGV LEVER ARM ON THE IGV TRUNNION CAN BE ROTATED BY 180° DURING INSTALLATION, BECAUSE THE SHAPE OF THE PARTS DOES NOT PREVENT THIS SUFFICIENTLY.  BASED ON THE MAINTENANCE RECORDS, IT CANNOT BE RULED OUT, THAT INDIVIDUAL IGVS REMAINED IN INCORRECTLY INSTALLED POSITION IN THE POTENTIALLY AFFECTED ENGINE POPULATION WITHOUT BEING NOTICED. MTU-H HAS REACHED OUT TO THE ORIGINAL EQUIPMENT MANUFACTURER (OEM) FOR TECHNICAL SUPPORT. THE OEM RECOMMENDED TO INSPECT POTENTIALLY AFFECTED ENGINES OF INCORRECT INSTALLED IGVS.
MISORIENTED IGVS CREATE ABNORMAL PERTURBATION INTO THE FLOW PATH. IT IS THE RECOMMENDATION TO GO BACK TO THE APPROVED CONFIGURATION AS SOON AS THE ISSUE IS DETECTED. THE OPERATION OF THE ENGINE CANNOT BE CONTINUED UNTIL THE NEXT SHOP VISIT AND NO DR OR CONTINUE IN SERVICE LIMIT CAN BE GRANTED IF IGV MISORIENTATION IS EVIDENCED.  OFF SCHEDULE VSV OPERATION IS DESCRIBED IN EM 72-00-00 INSPECTION 002, SUBTASK 72-00-00-220-089. ACCORDING TO THIS SUBTASK, THE LPC STAGE 5, HPC BLISK STAGE 1, AND HPC BLADES STAGE 2 SHALL BE REPLACED BEFORE ANY FURTHER OPERATION CAN TAKE PLACE. THIS SUBTASK DOES NOT CLEARLY PROVIDE INSTRUCTIONS FOR THOSE IGV OFF-SCHEDULE OPERATION. AS PART OF THE OEM RECOMMENDATION MTU HAS RECEIVED INSTRUCTIONS FOR PART DISPOSITION IN CASE INCORRECTLY INSTALLED IGVS ARE DETECTED.  THIS INCLUDES THAT ONLY THE HPC BLISK STAGE 1 AND HPC BLADES STAGE 2, AS WELL AS THE IMPACTED IGVS WITH LEVER ARMS AND ASSOCIATED HARDWARE, ALONG WITH BOTH ADJACENT IGVS (RIGHT AND LEFT) OF THE REVERSED IGV WITH LEVER ARMS AND ASSOCIATED HARDWARE, MUST BE DISCARDED REGARDLESS OF THEIR VISUAL CONDITION.

ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS:
A ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS WAS CONDUCTED BY MTU-H TO IDENTIFY THE PRIMARY CONTRIBUTORS TO THE CURRENT EVENT. THE ANALYSIS WAS PERFORMED USING AN ISHIKAWA DIAGRAM WHICH IDENTIFIED CONTRIBUTING FACTORS RELATED TO HUMAN FACTORS, MAINTENANCE PROCESSES, AND MATERIAL/DESIGN CHARACTERISTICS. 
MTU WORKPLANNING DEPARTMENT TRANSFERS THE OEM MANUAL REQUIREMENTS INTO INTERNAL WORKING DOCUMENTS (MASTERCARD) TO SUPPORT THE MECHANIC WITH BOTH, OEM INSTRUCTIONS BUT ALSO PROVIDE MTU EXPERIENCE AND EXPERTISE WHEN PERFORMING THE WORK.  THIS IS DESCRIBED IN OPH-04-05-07-04. THIS INTERNAL PROCEDURE REQUIRES THE WORK PLANNER TO REFERENCE ALL TECHNICAL DATA USED IN THE DOCUMENT TO ENSURE APPROPRIATE INCORPORATION OF CHANGES.
THE MASTERCARD FOR FAN HUB FRAME MODULE WAS COMPILED BASED ON OEM TASK TASK 72-23-00-040-001 (DISASSEMBLY) AND 72-23-00-440-001 (ASSEMBLY). THE TASKS WERE USED FOR BOTH, FBC AND FHF WORKSCOPES. IN 2016 THE SPECIAL PROCEDURE 014 WAS ISSUED, WHICH AT THAT POINT OF TIME CONTAINED THE SAME REQUIREMENTS AS THE EM TASK AND THEREFORE THE WORK PLANNER DID NOT SEE A NEED TO REFERENCE THE SPECIAL PROCEDURE IN THE WORK PLAN. IN 2022 THE OEM REVISED THE SPECIAL PROCEDURE 014. AS THERE WAS NO REFERENCE TO THE SPECIAL PROCEDURE IN THE EXISTING MASTERCARD, THE CHANGE WAS NOT PROPERLY DETECTED AND IT WAS INADVERTENTLY MISSED TO IMPLEMENT THE REVISED REQUIREMENTS FROM THE SPECIAL PROCEDURE INTO THE MASTERCARD. A CHANGE OF THE WORK PLAN WOULD HAVE INITIATED ADDITIONAL GATES AS A FOUR EYE CHECK AND A FIRST ARTICLE/FIRST BUILD PROCESS TO ENSURE PROPER IMPLEMENTATION OF THE OEM REQUIREMENTS. DUE TO THE MISSING REFERENCE TO SPECIAL PROCEDURE 014 NO CHANGE WAS MADE TO MTU MASTERCARD AND THE ERROR REMAINED UNDETECTED.  ESM 72-00-00 SPECIAL PROCEDURE 014 (IGV/VSV ACTUATING RINGS GUIDE PADS REPLACEMENT ON ENGINE OR PROPULSOR AT HORIZONTAL POSITION) WAS NOT YET INCLUDED IN THE MAINTENANCE PLANNING THUS HAVING NO INSTRUCTIONS IN THE TASK CARD. THIS WOULD HAVE INCLUDED A BORESCOPE INSPECTION OF ALL IGVS AFTER LEVER ARM INSTALLATION TO ENSURE CORRECT INSTALLATION. 
AT FAN BOOSTER COMPRESSOR (FBC) LEVEL, THE REQUIRED VISUAL INSPECTION (AS DEFINED IN THE APPLICABLE TASK CARD) COULD NOT BE PERFORMED AS DESCRIBED DUE TO ACCESSIBILITY LIMITATIONS.  THE USED TASK CARD WAS VALID FOR WORK AT FAN HUB FRAME MODULE LEVEL. THE TASK CARD WAS APPLIED AT FBC LEVEL EVEN THOUGH ITS INSPECTION REQUIREMENTS COULD NOT BE FULLY ACCOMPLISHED AT THIS STAGE DUE TO ACCESSIBILITY LIMITATIONS.  IN ADDITION, THE TRUNNION DESIGN INCORPORATES A SLIGHTLY CONICAL GEOMETRY FROM LEFT TO RIGHT. TRYOUTS SHOWED THAT NEVERTHELESS THE LEVER ARMS CAN BE MATED IN SEVERAL CASES TO THE TRUNNIONS IN WRONG DIRECTION LEADING TO THE DESCRIBED MISORIENTATION. THIS CONDITION CANNOT BE SEEN FROM EXTERNALLY.  EXTERNAL IDENTIFICATION WOULD BE POSSIBLE BY ACCORDING WITNESS MARKS ON THE LEVER ARMS AS WELL AS THE IGV TRUNNION/STUD. THIS IS ONLY PARTIALLY CONSIDERED IN THE GE90-100 ESM AS THERE IS NO INSTRUCTION TO APPLY THESE MARKS. A MATERIAL REVIEW SHOWED THAT NEITHER NEW NOR USED PARTS HAVE THESE MARKS. THIS HAS BEEN REPORTED BACK TO THE OEM IN 2024 WHO PLANNED AN UPDATED TO THE ESM IN ORDER TO RECOMMEND TO PUT THIS MARK DURING 72-23-00 FAN HUB FRAME ASSEMBLY. THIS UPDATE IS NOT PUBLISHED TO DATE. AS A PRECAUTION, MTU-H USES A THREAD PROTECTION BUSHING SCREWED ON EACH INDIVIDUAL IGV STUD TO PREVENT DAMAGES TO THE THREADS. THIS BUSHING ALSO IMPEDES FREE MOVEMENT WHEN THE IGV REMAINS INSTALLED IN THE FHF.  ALL WORK PLANNERS WERE INFORMED ABOUT THIS ISSUE TO REMIND THEM OF THE IMPORTANCE OF SPECIAL PROCEDURES AND THEIR INCORPORATION INTO THE MASTERCARDS. THE INTERNAL PROCEDURE WILL BE REVIEWED AND IMPROVED ACCORDINGLY TO PROVIDE IMPROVED INSTRUCTION ON REFLECTING THE REFERENCES OF INCORPORATED DOCUMENTS SUCH AS SPECIAL PROCEDURES.  ALL SPECIAL PROCEDURES WILL BE REVIEWED FOR CORRECT IMPLEMENTATION.  MTU-H HAS REVISED THE MASTERCARD AND IMPLEMENTED A MANDATORY 360-DEGREE BORESCOPE INSPECTION (BSI) OF THE IGVS FOLLOWING LEVER ARM REINSTALLATION IN ACCORDANCE WITH GE90-100 ESM 72-00-00 SPECIAL PROCEDURES 014, SUBTASK 72-00-00-220-384 AS A STANDARD PROCEDURE FOR FUTURE ENGINES UNDERGOING THE APPLICABLE WORK SCOPE.
